quoted: On a device where vertical positioning is applicable and the ADVANCING phrase is not specified, automatic advancing will be provided by the implementor to act as if the user had specified AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE [GR14, OK]; If vertical positioning is not applicable on the device, the MCS will ignore the vertical positioning specified or implied [GR12, OK]
reason: A test exists whose expectation holds under BOTH determinations and which a real GR14 violation would fail: the same messages sent with no ADVANCING to D1 and with AFTER ADVANCING 1 LINE to D2 must leave byte-identical device files (GR14's 'act as if' if positioning applies; GR12 ignores both if it does not). It fails if a device ever honours ADVANCING with any other default, which is exactly the contingency the derivation would leave to re-adjudication. The derivation's premise is also not decisive: the project's own signed DRV-GR-14.9.11.4-11 calls line-structured streams devices 'on which vertical positioning IS applicable', while 3.3 calls the line-structured <name>.out not applicable; the two determinations must be reconciled. No defect: today ADVANCING 3 LINES, BEFORE ADVANCING PAGE and ADVANCING 0 are ignored (send2 probe), consistent with GR12. The witness needs a harness test (two destinations in mcs.json, read D1.out/D2.out), as PB5373 class 4 does for the MCS.

quoted: permits the choice of either the second or subsequent characters appearing superimposed
reason: Every device is one kind: McsStore.Transmit appends Concat(segments)+NewLine at the committed end; MessageDefinitions.Devices is the closed set (terminals and destinations without deliverTo), all <name>.out. Nothing writes a CR overstrike or repositions, ADVANCING 0 is ignored (send2: GGGGG and HHHHH on their own lines with AFTER ADVANCING 0 LINES REPLACING LINE), so no device can present two characters at one position and none offers the REPLACING/superimpose choice. Any test would witness GR12/GR17/GR18 behaviour, never GR16's two arms, which need a device that offers both. Contingent on Transmit staying the only device writer; the Names cell should cite it.

quoted: When a receiving communication device does not support the superimposition of two or more characters at the same position [GR18, OK] ... the characters transmitted by the SEND statement replace all characters which may have previously been transmitted to the same line beginning with the leftmost character position of the line; each message or message segment will begin on the next available character position of the communication device [GR2, OK]
reason: The derivation's key step is false: a message of several segments is several SENDs on ONE line. Probe send2: SEND DDD WITH ESI, SEND EEEEE WITH ESI, SEND FF WITH EMI leave the single line 'DDDEEEEEFF', so the second and third SENDs did transmit characters to a line that already held characters, on a device whose antecedent (no superimposition) is TRUE. Reading 1 (literal GR18): those SENDs' characters 'replace all characters which may have previously been transmitted to the same line beginning with the leftmost character position', so the line should not read DDDEEEEEFF; that is a defect and a test (this program) witnesses it. Reading 2 (GR2 governs a variable-length device): 'each message or message segment will begin on the next available character position', so no two characters ever share a position, GR18 is vacuous, and DDDEEEEEFF conforms; the derivation then stands only if rewritten on GR2, not on 'one message is one line'. Reading 2 is the likelier intent (GR16-18 concern repositioning onto a used line), but the text does not decide it. The same false step is in the CONFORMS note of 1985-GR-XIV.3.6.4-17 ('no earlier characters share its line').
